title: Halal-NeSyNet: Clause-Scoped Neuro-Symbolic Cross-Attention for Automated Food Ingredient Auditing and Risk-Aware Halal Logistics Triage
abstract: arXiv:2611.01612v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Verifying that a packaged food is Halal requires reading ingredient declarations and E-number additives before goods enter certified warehouses. Dual-origin additives such as E471, E422, E441 and E920 are Mushbooh (doubtful) unless a botanical, microbial or certified-Halal qualifier appears in the same ingredient clause, so a plant-based qualifier on one clause must not clear an unqualified additive in another. We call a failure to respect this scope cross-clause modifier confounding and build a benchmark of 3,199 items (277 Open Food Facts records and 2,922 template-generated clause-swap items, labelled by an explicit 50-code rule base rather than by a certification authority) with a 540-item counterfactual suite. We propose Halal-NeSyNet, which couples a DistilBERT encoder with a 16-dimensional rule-derived symbolic vector through cross-attention and gated fusion, trained with an asymmetric false-Halal risk loss. translated_title: Halal-NeSyNet：面向自动化食品成分审计与风险感知清真物流分诊的子句范围神经符号交叉注意力
translated_abstract: 验证包装食品是否符合清真标准，需要在货物进入认证仓库之前阅读成分声明和E编码添加剂。E471、E422、E441和E920等双来源添加剂属于Mushbooh（存疑）状态，除非在同一成分子句中出现植物来源、微生物来源或认证清真的限定词，因此某一个子句上的植物来源限定词不能用于判定另一个子句中缺乏限定词的添加剂是否合规。我们将违反这一范围约束的失败称为“跨子句修饰词混淆”，并构建了一个包含3,199个条目的基准数据集（277条Open Food Facts记录和2,922条模板生成的子句交换条目，由显式的50条编码规则库而非认证机构进行标注），以及一个包含540个条目的反事实测试集。我们提出Halal-NeSyNet，该方法将DistilBERT编码器与16维规则衍生符号向量通过交叉注意力和门控融合相结合，并使用非对称的假清真风险损失进行训练。在五个随机种子上，文本……（原文摘要至此被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出Halal-NeSyNet模型，通过将DistilBERT编码器与规则衍生符号向量进行子句范围的交叉注意力与门控融合，解决清真食品成分审核中跨子句修饰词混淆问题，并构建了包含3,199个条目的基准数据集以实现自动化食品成分审计和风险感知的清真物流分诊。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes Halal-NeSyNet, which couples a DistilBERT encoder with a 16-dimensional rule-derived symbolic vector through clause-scoped cross-attention and gated fusion, trained with an asymmetric false-Halal risk loss, to prevent cross-clause modifier confounding in Halal ingredient auditing, supported by a 3,199-item benchmark and a 540-item counterfactual suite.
